relations.rationale: Dara's arrival timing relative to Esme has no bearing on team assignments.
Arrival order says nothing about age.
Arrival timing has no connection to the number of teams.
Dara being out of breath has nothing to do with who brought the first-aid kit.
Dara's breathlessness is unrelated to whether Jun made it before departure.
Dara jogging has no bearing on Jun's age.
Dara's physical state is unrelated to Esme and Eli's team assignments.
One person's brief breathlessness upon arrival doesn't indicate the group's overall end-of-day feelings.
Being taller than most of the group directly explains why his height would be useful for spotting distant markers.
Eli's usefulness for spotting markers has no bearing on his and Esme's team membership.
Eli's height utility is unrelated to the group's overall mood at the end.
Who brought the first-aid kit has no connection to Jun's wrong turn.
Yara bringing supplies is unrelated to Esme and Eli's team assignments.
Both actions show Yara being responsible and prepared, suggesting a consistent character trait, though not strictly logically linked.
Jun arriving last is consistent with and explained by having taken a wrong turn, supporting that account.
Jun arriving last among individuals doesn't preclude him still arriving before the group departed.
Arriving last doesn't inherently affect Jun's ability to later set the pace.
Jun's arrival order is unrelated to weather-driven pace changes later.
Taking a wrong turn could delay Jun but doesn't determine whether he still made it before departure.
Jun's wrong turn is unrelated to whether Dara and Eli were on different teams.
